questions.question: What is the difference between Azure RBAC and Azure AD roles?
options: They are identical

Azure RBAC: controls access to Azure resources (VM, storage, RG). Azure AD roles: control Azure AD directory operations (user admin, global admin). RBAC scope: management group, subscription, RG, resource.
questions.explanation: RBAC: Owner, Contributor, Reader on Azure resources. AD roles: Global Admin, User Admin, Security Admin in Azure AD tenant. Global Admin ≠ Owner of Azure subscription (separate assignment required).

questions.question: What is a VNet peering vs VPN Gateway in Azure?
options: They are identical

VNet peering: private, low-latency, non-transitive L2-like connectivity between VNets in same/different regions (no internet). VPN Gateway: encrypted tunnel over internet/ExpressRoute — transitive if hub-spoke topology with BGP.
questions.explanation: VNet peering: no bandwidth limits, low latency, no gateway needed. Non-transitive: A↔B, B↔C doesn't enable A↔C. Virtual WAN or NVA routes transit traffic. VPN Gateway: internet-based, encrypted, supports on-premises.

questions.question: What is an Azure NSG (Network Security Group)?
options: A firewall appliance

Stateful Layer 4 firewall rules attached to subnets or NICs. Contains inbound/outbound security rules with priority (100-4096), lower number = higher priority. Default rules allow VNet traffic, deny internet inbound.
questions.explanation: NSG rules: priority (100-4096), source/dest (IP, service tag, ASG), port, protocol, allow/deny. Applied to subnet or NIC (both evaluated if both attached). Service Tags: Azure services without listing IPs (Storage, SQL, etc.).

questions.question: What is Azure Bastion and why is it preferred over Jump Boxes?
options: Bastion is a type of VM
Managed PaaS RDP/SSH over HTTPS in Azure Portal — no public IP on VMs, no NSG rule needed for 3389/22, provides browser-based access with session recording capabilities (Standard tier).
questions.explanation: Traditional jump box: VM with public IP as intermediary, needs patching, single point of failure. Azure Bastion: managed, always-available, browser-based, audit logs, Standard tier adds ShareableLink and session monitoring.

questions.question: What are Azure Availability Sets?
options: Same as Availability Zones
Groups VMs across fault domains (different physical racks/power/network) and update domains (VMs not rebooted simultaneously during maintenance) — provides HA within a single data center.
questions.explanation: Availability Sets: up to 3 fault domains, 20 update domains. Free to use. VMs get different fault/update domain assignments. Azure SLA: 99.95% for 2+ VMs in same Availability Set. Different from AZs (separate buildings).

questions.question: What is Azure managed disk types — Standard HDD, Standard SSD, Premium SSD, Ultra Disk?
options: All have the same performance

Standard HDD: cheapest, variable latency (test/dev). Standard SSD: consistent latency, entry production. Premium SSD: high IOPS/throughput (most production). Ultra Disk: sub-ms latency, configure IOPS/throughput at runtime.
questions.explanation: Standard HDD: cost-optimized dev/test. Standard SSD: web servers, lightly used prod. Premium SSD: SQL Server, business apps (needs DS/GS/FS VM sizes). Ultra Disk: SAP HANA, top-tier databases — max 160,000 IOPS.

questions.question: What is Azure AD Connect and what does it do?
options: An Azure AD service only
Syncs on-premises Active Directory to Azure AD — enables hybrid identity: same username/password for cloud and on-premises. Sync modes: Password Hash Sync, Pass-through Auth, Federation (AD FS).
questions.explanation: Azure AD Connect sync: users, groups, passwords (hashes) from on-prem AD to Azure AD. PHS: simplest (hash synced). PTA: authentication happens on-prem (no hash in cloud). Federation: AD FS for full on-prem auth.

questions.question: What is a user-defined route (UDR) in Azure?
options: A DNS entry
A custom route table entry that overrides Azure's default system routes — used to route traffic through an NVA (firewall), force-tunnel to on-premises, or control traffic between subnets.
questions.explanation: UDR overrides Azure system routes. Next hop types: Virtual Appliance (NVA IP), VNet Gateway (for VPN force-tunnel), None (drops traffic), Internet. Applied to subnets. 0.0.0.0/0 → NVA forces all traffic through firewall.

questions.question: What is Azure Application Gateway WAF?
options: A DNS protection service
An OSI Layer 7 load balancer with Web Application Firewall — protects against OWASP Top 10 attacks (SQLi, XSS), supports URL-based routing, SSL termination, session affinity.
questions.explanation: App Gateway: like AWS ALB + WAF combined. WAF policies: Prevention mode (blocks) vs Detection mode (logs only). Custom rules + OWASP managed rules. SKUs: Standard_v2, WAF_v2. Supports AKS Ingress Controller.

questions.question: What is Azure Monitor Log Analytics workspace?
options: A separate product from Azure Monitor
The storage and query engine within Azure Monitor where logs are collected and analyzed using Kusto Query Language (KQL) — data sources: VMs, AKS, security logs, custom logs.
questions.explanation: Log Analytics workspace: central log repository. KQL query: 'AzureActivity | where OperationName contains 'delete' | summarize count() by Caller'. Solutions: Security Center, Container Insights, VM Insights all store data here.

questions.question: What is an Azure Storage Account access tier — Hot, Cool, Archive?
options: No difference in cost

Hot: frequent access (highest storage cost, lowest access cost). Cool: infrequent access (lower storage, higher access cost, 30-day min). Archive: rarely accessed (lowest storage, highest retrieval cost, hours to rehydrate).
questions.explanation: Lifecycle management policies auto-tier objects. Archive retrieval: Rehydrate to Hot/Cool (hours) or use priority retrieval (1 hour max). Archive tier: Flexible (15h), High (1h), Standard (15h - cheapest rehydration). Only blob tier can use Archive.

questions.question: What is Azure Private Endpoint vs Service Endpoint?
options: They are identical

Service Endpoint: extends VNet identity to Azure service over Azure backbone (source IP = VNet). Private Endpoint: creates a private IP inside your VNet for the service — fully private, accessible from on-premises via ExpressRoute.
questions.explanation: Service Endpoint: traffic stays on Azure backbone, service can restrict to specific VNets, but service still has public endpoint. Private Endpoint: assigns private IP in VNet, DNS resolves to private IP, accessible from anywhere with network connectivity.

questions.question: What is Azure Disk Encryption vs Server-Side Encryption (SSE)?
options: They are identical

SSE: Azure encrypts disk data at rest automatically at the storage level (AES-256, free). Azure Disk Encryption (ADE): encrypts VM OS/data disks using BitLocker (Windows) or dm-crypt (Linux) at the VM level, keys in Key Vault.
questions.explanation: SSE: transparent, automatic, no performance impact. ADE: additional layer encrypting at OS level, protects against stolen physical disk. Double encryption: SSE + ADE for highest security. Customer-Managed Keys via Key Vault optional for both.

questions.question: What is Azure Automation DSC (Desired State Configuration)?
options: A deployment script runner
A configuration management service using PowerShell DSC to ensure Windows/Linux VMs maintain their desired configuration — detects and corrects configuration drift automatically.
questions.explanation: Azure Automation DSC: pull-based configuration, nodes check in every 15-30 minutes. DSC configurations define: installed software, registry settings, services running, file contents. Reporting shows compliant vs non-compliant nodes.

questions.question: What is Azure Policy initiative (policy set)?
options: A single policy
A collection of related Azure Policy definitions grouped together for assignment as a single unit — simplifies assigning multiple related policies (e.g., 'CIS Microsoft Azure Foundations Benchmark').
questions.explanation: Initiatives bundle policies. Built-in initiatives: CIS, NIST, ISO 27001, PCI DSS. Custom initiatives: group your organization's policies. Assignment scope: management group, subscription, resource group. Remediation tasks fix non-compliant resources.

questions.question: What is the difference between Azure backup vault and Recovery Services vault?
options: Backup vault is newer, Recovery Services vault supports older workloads. Backup vault: Azure Blobs, Disks, PostgreSQL. Recovery Services vault: Azure VMs, SQL in VM, SAP HANA, Files, on-premises (MARS/MABS).
They are identical
questions.explanation: Recovery Services vault: supports most workloads (VMs, on-premises via MARS agent, Azure Files, SQL). Backup vault: newer resource, supports blob/disk/PostgreSQL backup. Both can hold backup data with replication options (LRS, ZRS, GRS).

questions.question: What is Azure AD Conditional Access?
options: A network ACL

Policies that evaluate signals (user, location, device, app, risk) and enforce access controls — allow, block, or require MFA based on conditions. Example: require MFA when user accesses from untrusted location.
questions.explanation: Conditional Access signals: user/group, IP location, device compliance (Intune), application, sign-in risk (Identity Protection). Controls: block, allow, require MFA, require compliant device. Requires Azure AD Premium P1+.

questions.question: What is an Azure subscription's default vCPU quota per region?
options: Unlimited
Default quota is 20 vCPUs per region per VM family. Request increases via Subscriptions → Usage + quotas in Portal. Quotas vary by region, VM family, and subscription type.
questions.explanation: Azure quotas (soft limits): 20 vCPUs default per region per subscription. Request increases in Portal under Subscriptions. Important for auto-scaling deployments that might hit limits. Monitor with Azure Monitor quota metrics.

questions.question: What is Azure AD Privileged Identity Management (PIM)?
options: A user provisioning tool
Provides just-in-time (JIT) privileged access to Azure AD roles and Azure resources — users request elevation, get time-limited assignments with approval workflow and audit trail.
questions.explanation: PIM reduces standing privileged access. Instead of permanent Global Admin: activate role for 1 hour when needed with justification, optional MFA, approval required, all activations logged. Requires Azure AD Premium P2.

questions.question: What is Azure Load Balancer SKU Standard vs Basic?
options: Identical functionality

Standard: supports AZs, backend pools with VMs in multiple AZs, HTTPS health probes, 1000 rules, HA ports, secure by default (needs NSG). Basic: AZ-unaware, 300 instances, no HTTPS probes, no SLA for single VM.
questions.explanation: Standard LB is the recommended SKU: built-in HA across AZs, outbound rules for SNAT, 99.99% SLA with 2+ VMs. Basic is being deprecated. Cannot mix Standard and Basic LB in the same availability set.

questions.question: What are Azure management locks and what types exist?
options: Network security locks
Resource locks prevent accidental deletion or modification: CanNotDelete (can read/modify, cannot delete), ReadOnly (can read only, cannot modify or delete). Inherited by child resources.
questions.explanation: Locks apply to: subscription, RG, resource. CanNotDelete: prevent accidental deletion while allowing updates. ReadOnly: treat resource like a Reader role (no modifications). Applied via Portal, CLI, Bicep. Override requires Owner + lock removal.

questions.question: What is Azure DNS Private Zones?
options: A public DNS service
Provides DNS name resolution for resources within VNets without exposing DNS records publicly — auto-registration adds VM DNS records, linked VNets can query the zone.
questions.explanation: Private DNS Zone: e.g., 'internal.contoso.com'. Link to VNets (with/without autoregistration). VMs register their FQDN automatically if autoregistration enabled. Resolves across VNets if all linked. No custom DNS server needed.

questions.question: What is Azure Storage redundancy types?
options: Only one redundancy type
LRS: 3 copies in one datacenter. ZRS: 3 copies across 3 AZs in one region. GRS: LRS + async copy to paired region. GZRS: ZRS + async copy to paired region. RA variants: readable from secondary.
questions.explanation: LRS (cheapest, 99.999999999%): single DC. ZRS (99.9999999999%): three DCs same region. GRS: primary LRS + secondary LRS in paired region. GZRS: primary ZRS + secondary. RA-GRS/RA-GZRS: read access to secondary endpoint.

questions.question: What is Azure Container Instances (ACI) vs AKS?
options: They are the same service

ACI: run single containers or small container groups without orchestration — fastest to deploy, per-second billing, no cluster management. AKS: full managed Kubernetes for production containerized apps at scale.
questions.explanation: ACI: good for burst/batch, isolated containers, event-driven workloads. No persistent storage orchestration. AKS: production containers with HA, rolling updates, service mesh, KEDA, autoscaling. ACI can be used as virtual nodes in AKS.

questions.question: What is Azure Diagnostic Settings?
options: A hardware diagnostic tool
Configures where to send Azure resource diagnostic data: Azure Monitor Logs (Log Analytics), Azure Storage (archival), Event Hub (SIEM streaming), partner solutions.
questions.explanation: Diagnostic settings: per-resource configuration specifying which logs/metrics to collect and where to send them. Platform logs: resource logs (resource activities), activity log (subscription operations). Enable for compliance and troubleshooting.

questions.question: What is Azure AD External Identities?
options: Guest accounts only
Allows external users (other Azure AD tenants, social IDs, email OTP) to access your Azure AD tenant's apps. Includes: B2B (collaborate with partners) and B2C (customer identities).
questions.explanation: B2B (Business-to-Business): invite partner users as Guests, they sign in with their own identity. B2C: build customer identity for your apps (separate Azure AD B2C tenant). Governs access to apps not directory management.

questions.question: What is Azure ExpressRoute Global Reach?
options: ExpressRoute for small businesses
Connects two on-premises networks via Azure's network backbone through their respective ExpressRoute circuits — enables branch-to-branch connectivity without backhaul to on-premises.
questions.explanation: Global Reach: Site A → ExpressRoute → Azure → ExpressRoute → Site B. Traffic stays on Microsoft backbone. Useful for: connecting remote offices through Azure, replacing expensive MPLS WAN, DR site connectivity.

questions.question: What is a scale set instance protection policy?
options: Prevents all instance changes

Protects specific scale set instances from scale-in operations — either 'protect from scale-in' (don't remove this instance during scale-in) or 'protect from set actions' (also protects from manual changes).
questions.explanation: Instance protection: useful for long-running jobs. 'ProtectFromScaleIn': instance won't be removed by auto-scale. 'ProtectFromSetActions': also excludes from manual reimage/upgrade operations. Set per-instance via REST API or CLI.

questions.question: What is Azure VM Extensions?
options: VM plug-in cards
Small software components that run on Azure VMs for post-deployment configuration: DSC, Custom Script, Log Analytics agent, Antimalware, Diagnostics, AAD login, Azure Monitor for VMs.
questions.explanation: Extensions automate VM configuration after deployment. Custom Script Extension: runs PowerShell/Bash scripts. DSC Extension: applies DSC configuration. Managed via ARM/Bicep, Portal, CLI. Multiple extensions can run on one VM.

questions.question: What is Azure Update Manager?
options: A Windows Update for all VMs tool
A unified platform for managing, scheduling, and reporting on OS updates for Azure VMs and Arc-enabled on-premises servers — assesses patch compliance, schedules maintenance windows.
questions.explanation: Azure Update Manager (replaced Automation Update Management): centralized patching for Windows/Linux VMs across Azure, AWS, GCP (via Arc). Maintenance configurations: schedule patching windows. Assessment: see missing patches without installing.

questions.question: What is Azure Front Door?
options: A DNS service
Global load balancer and CDN combining: global HTTP load balancing, SSL offload, application acceleration, WAF, and CDN — routes users to the lowest-latency/healthiest backend.
questions.explanation: Front Door: Layer 7 global routing using anycast. Origins: Azure or external backends. Routing methods: latency, priority, weight, session affinity. WAF policies at global entry point. Unlike Traffic Manager (DNS-based), Front Door operates at L7.

questions.question: What is the Azure Activity Log?
options: An application performance log
An audit log of subscription-level management operations: who created/deleted/modified which resource, when, from which IP — retained for 90 days by default, exportable to Log Analytics/Storage.
questions.explanation: Activity Log: records Azure control plane actions. Categories: Administrative (CRUD), Security, Service Health, Alert, Policy, Recommendation. Key fields: caller (UPN/SP), operation, result (succeeded/failed), timestamp. Alert on critical operations.

questions.question: What is Azure NetApp Files?
options: A blob storage service
An enterprise-grade NAS (NFS/SMB) service powered by NetApp hardware — high-performance, low-latency file storage for SAP HANA, HPC, Oracle databases, and VDI workloads.
questions.explanation: Azure NetApp Files: enterprise NAS with sub-millisecond latency. Service levels: Standard (16 MB/s/TiB), Premium (64 MB/s/TiB), Ultra (128 MB/s/TiB). Supports NFS v3/v4.1 and SMB 3.x. Cross-region replication for DR.

questions.question: What is Azure Defender for Cloud (formerly Security Center)?
options: A basic firewall product
A unified security management and advanced threat protection system — provides security posture score, vulnerability assessments for VMs/containers/databases, and threat detection with alerts.
questions.explanation: Defender for Cloud: CSPM (Cloud Security Posture Management) free tier. Enhanced protections (paid): Defender for Servers, Containers, SQL, Storage, DNS. Secure Score: percentage of security recommendations implemented.

questions.question: What is Azure Automation Runbook?
options: A printed operations manual
A PowerShell, Python, or graphical workflow automated via Azure Automation — runs scheduled or webhook-triggered tasks: VM start/stop, resource cleanup, patch management, configuration changes.
questions.explanation: Runbooks: PowerShell/Python scripts stored in Azure Automation account. Run on Hybrid Runbook Worker (on-prem) or Azure sandbox. Scheduling, webhooks, and event grid triggers. Used for routine ops automation and remediation.
